title: If a late field loses yield instead of failing a hard deadline, does a scout-and-treater fleet still lose to inline weeding robots?
lede: replaces the hard deadline of osrobot-deadline with a 2% yield loss per leaf stage of delay (Knezevic et al. 2003): the best pipeline costs 1.06 to 1.20 times the best inline fleet at 0.72 ha and 1.49 to 1.51 at 0.18 ha, and at 1.62 ha inline is cheaper when the window closes by 8 h and the pipeline from 12 h
summary: A stdlib extension of osrobot-deadline (no new simulation; fleet prices still assumed round numbers) that charges each late field 2% of its revenue per leaf stage of delay past the window, the pooled corn and soybean figure of Knezevic, Evans & Mainz (2003, Crop Management 2(1)). Leaf-stage length (2, 4, 8 days), an 8 h working day and revenue (1,000 and 2,000 USD/ha) are swept, not sourced. For 16 equal fields the fleet minimising fleet cost plus lost yield is searched over up to four scouts, 16 treaters and 32 inline robots. Pipeline over inline cost is 1.06 to 1.20 at 0.72 ha and 1.49 to 1.51 at 0.18 ha in every cell; at 1.62 ha it ranges 0.89 to 1.18, with inline cheaper when the window closes by 8 h (12.27 against 13.07 USD/ha at 2,000 USD/ha revenue and a 4-day stage) and the pipeline cheaper from 12 h. Late loss reaches 8.56 USD/ha in the worst cell against about 12 of fleet cost. Limits: the 2% rate is for corn and soybean up to canopy closure and is applied linearly; stage length and revenue unsourced; equal fields, one window, no weather or failures; search capped at four scouts.
